Indian Patent Office / Ministry of AYUSH
content: 3. What are not inventions.—The following are not inventions within the meaning of this Act,—

authority: Indian Patent Office / Ministry of AYUSH
content: (a) an invention which is frivolous or which claims anything obviously contrary to well established natural laws;

authority: Indian Patent Office / Ministry of AYUSH
content: (b) an invention the primary or intended use or commercial exploitation of which could be contrary to public order or morality or which causes serious prejudice to human, animal or plant life or health or to the environment;

authority: Indian Patent Office / Ministry of AYUSH
content: (c) the mere discovery of a scientific principle or the formulation of an abstract theory or discovery of any living thing or non-living substance occurring in nature;

authority: Indian Patent Office / Ministry of AYUSH
content: (d) the mere discovery of a new form of a known substance which does not result in the enhancement of the known efficacy of that substance or the mere discovery of any new property or new use for a known substance or of the mere use of a known process, machine or apparatus unless such known process results in a new product or employs at least one new reactant;

authority: Indian Patent Office / Ministry of AYUSH
content: (e) a substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components thereof or a process for producing such substance;

authority: Indian Patent Office / Ministry of AYUSH
content: (j) plants and animals in whole or any part thereof other than micro-organisms but including seeds, varieties and species and essentially biological processes for production or propagation of plants and animals;

authority: Indian Patent Office / Ministry of AYUSH
content:
(p) an invention which in effect is traditional knowledge or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known component or components.

# CHAPTER IV-A: PROVISIONS RELATING TO AYURVEDIC, SIDDHA AND UNANI DRUGS

authority: Indian Patent Office / Ministry of AYUSH
content: Rule 158B. Guidelines for issue of license with respect to Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani drugs.—

authority: Indian Patent Office / Ministry of AYUSH
content: (1) Patent or Proprietary medicine in relation to Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani systems of medicine includes all formulations containing only such ingredients mentioned in the formulae described in the authoritative books of Ayurveda, Siddha or Unani systems specified in the First Schedule.

authority: Indian Patent Office / Ministry of AYUSH
content: (2) Proof of effectiveness for licensing of Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani drugs:

authority: Indian Patent Office / Ministry of AYUSH
content: (a) Traditional use: For classical drugs listed in authoritative texts, no safety or efficacy study is required if manufactured strictly according to the formula.

authority: Indian Patent Office / Ministry of AYUSH
content: (b) Modified/New Formulations: For patent or proprietary medicine, proof of safety and effectiveness as specified by the licensing authority (Schedule T GMP compliance) shall be submitted.
